title: IUCN Species

sections.title: Page 1
sections.text:
IUCN Species
IUCN Categories Meaning
   •   Extinct (EX): No living individuals remain after exhaustive surveys.
       (Wikipedia)
   •   Extinct in the Wild (EW): Survives only in captivity or outside its
       historical range. (Wikipedia)
   •   Critically Endangered (CR): Faces an extremely high risk of extinction
       in the wild. (cmsdocs.s3.amazonaws.com, Wikipedia)
   •   Endangered (EN): Faces a very high risk of extinction in the wild.
       (cmsdocs.s3.amazonaws.com, Wikipedia)
   •   Vulnerable (VU): Faces a high risk of extinction in the wild.
       (cmsdocs.s3.amazonaws.com, Wikipedia)
   •   Near Threatened (NT): Close to qualifying as threatened; likely to
       become so soon. (cmsdocs.s3.amazonaws.com, Wikipedia)
   •   Least Concern (LC): Widespread and abundant; not at immediate risk.
       (cmsdocs.s3.amazonaws.com, Wikipedia)
   •   Data Deficient (DD): Insufficient data for assessment; not a threat
       category. (cmsdocs.s3.amazonaws.com, Wikipedia)
   •   Not    Evaluated    (NE):   Not     yet        assessed     by    IUCN.
       (cmsdocs.s3.amazonaws.com, Wikipedia)
'Threatened' refers collectively to CR, EN, and VU. (Wikipedia, IUCN Red List)

World Example Species
  •   CR: Javan rhinoceros (Rhinoceros sondaicus), a mammal native to Java
      (2021–22); Sumatran rhinoceros (Dicerorhinus sumatrensis), mammal in
      Sumatra and NE India (2015); Vaquita (Phocoena sinus), porpoise in the
      Gulf of California (2018); Hawksbill sea turtle (Eretmochelys imbricata),
      marine reptile in tropical oceans (2008); Saola (Pseudoryx nghetinhensis),
      mammal from the Annamite Range (2015).
  •   EN: Tiger (Panthera tigris), mammal across Asia (2021); African savanna
      elephant (Loxodonta africana), mammal in sub-Saharan Africa (2021);
      Blue whale (Balaenoptera musculus), marine mammal worldwide (2018);
      African wild dog (Lycaon pictus), mammal in Africa (2012); Wild water
      buffalo (Bubalus arnee), mammal in South/Southeast Asia (2016).
  •   VU: Leopard (Panthera pardus), mammal in Africa and Asia (2016);
      Giraffe spp., mammal in Africa (2016/2020–21); Hippopotamus
      (Hippopotamus amphibius), mammal in Africa (2016); Lion (Panthera
      leo), mammal in Africa and Asia (2016); Koala (Phascolarctos cinereus),
      mammal in Australia (2022).

India Example Species
  •   CR: Great Indian bustard (Ardeotis nigriceps), bird in central India (2018);
      Jerdon’s courser (Rhinoptilus bitorquatus), bird in Andhra Pradesh (2018);

      White-rumped vulture (Gyps bengalensis), bird in the Indian subcontinent

  •   EN: Asian elephant (Elephas maximus), mammal in India/South Asia
      (2020–21); Red panda (Ailurus fulgens), mammal in the Eastern Himalayas
      (2015); Ganges river dolphin (Platanista gangetica), cetacean in the
      Ganges–Brahmaputra system (2012); Lion-tailed macaque (Macaca
      silenus), mammal in the Western Ghats (2015); Wild water buffalo
      (Bubalus arnee), mammal in NE India and Bangladesh (2016).

sections.title: Page 7
sections.text:
Notes & Context
  •   The IUCN Red List includes nine categories from Extinct (EX) to Not
      Evaluated (NE) (IUCN Red List, iucn.org).
  •   Extinct in the Wild (EW) species, such as Père David’s deer and
      Wyoming toad, survive only under controlled human care or limited
      reintroduction programs (Wikipedia).
  •   The Extinct category includes notable species like the dodo, Steller’s sea
      cow, and woolly mammoth, as compiled in the IUCN’s records (Wikipedia,
      A-Z Animals).
  •   For Critically Endangered (CR), species like the vaquita and saola are
      among the most imperiled mammals; amphibian examples include the
      Kihansi spray toad (Wikipedia).

Highlights & Conservation Context
  •   Extinct (EX) and Extinct in the Wild (EW) designations underscore
      irreversible biodiversity loss or reliance on human care. Govenia floridana
      is fully extinct, whereas species like Franklinia alatamaha and
      Encephalartos woodii survive only in cultivation or managed conservation
      settings. (Wikipedia)
  •   Critically Endangered (CR) examples showcase highly restricted
      endemics, often surviving only on tiny cliffs or isolated habitats—ranging
      from Mediterranean sea cliffs to Puerto Rican limestone hills. Such species
      face extreme threats from habitat loss, grazing, or collection. (Wikipedia,
      top50.iucn-mpsg.org, gardensillustrated.com)
  •   Endangered (EN) examples illustrate regionally significant species under
      grave threat from human pressures, such as overharvesting (Aconitum
      chasmanthum) or disease (Ulmus americana). (iucn.org, topicwise.in)
  •   Vulnerable (VU): Paris polyphylla reflects medicinally valued species in
      high-altitude fragile ecosystems. Conservation actions to reintroduce it are
      already underway in the Himalayas. (The Times of India)
  •   Near Threatened (NT) plants like Madhuca barbata, M. dubardii, and M.
      pallida are small trees in the Sapotaceae family found in Southeast Asian
      dipterocarp forests—habitats under strong threat from logging and palm-
      oil-driven land conversion (Wikipedia).
  •   Goniothalamus wynaadensis, endemic to India’s Western Ghats with
      limited distribution, is also assessed NT, threatened by habitat
      fragmentation (Wikipedia).
  •   Data Deficient (DD) entries often involve lesser-studied or narrow-range
      taxa such as aquatic Charophyta algae or Isoetes quillworts—reflecting
      gaps in data rather than lack of threat (Wikipedia).
